title: Borodin's light triangles in planar graphs of minimum degree five
abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of Borodin's theorem on light triangles, for finite simple graphs with the combinatorial planarity (genus-zero rotation systems) of the registered entry Kuratowski's theorem. The weight of a triangle is the sum of the degrees of its vertices. Every plane map of a graph of minimum degree at least five has a face of length three of weight at most 17 (light_face), and hence a planar graph of minimum degree at least five has a triangle of weight at most 17 (light_triangle). Two statements. The proof is a discharging argument run on the rotation system, with face charges in place of an edge-maximal counterexample; the local analysis at 5-vertices (32768 configurations of neighbour degrees capped at eight and corner types) is checked by decide in the kernel.
